paragraphs.text: Pedestrian crossings with traffic lights were first introduced to reduce accidents, but their design has changed a great deal since then. Early crossings gave walkers a fixed amount of time, which many older people found too short.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Modern crossings in several cities use sensors that detect when someone is still in the road and keep the traffic lights red until they reach the pavement. In trials, this reduced the number of people still crossing when cars began to move by more than half.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Countdown timers, which show how many seconds are left, have had mixed results. They helped pedestrians decide whether to start crossing, but some drivers used them to judge when to speed up, which increased the risk to people who crossed late.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Sound signals were added to help people with poor sight. Some cities now use a different sound for each direction of the crossing, so that users know which way it is safe to walk.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Researchers stress that crossings work best when they are placed where people actually want to cross. If a crossing is too far from shops or bus stops, many pedestrians simply cross elsewhere.
paragraphs.label: E

items.quote: Pedestrian crossings with traffic lights were first introduced to reduce accidents

explanation.en: “were first introduced to reduce accidents” → A. E contradicts the text: older people found the time too short.
explanation.kk: «were first introduced to reduce accidents» → A. E мәтінге қайшы: қарт адамдарға уақыт жетпеген.
explanation.ru: «were first introduced to reduce accidents» → A. E противоречит тексту: пожилым времени как раз не хватало.

items.quote: this reduced the number of people still crossing when cars began to move by more than half

explanation.en: Sensors keep the light red until people reach the pavement, and those still in the road were “reduced … by more than half” → F.
explanation.kk: Сенсор жаяу адам өтіп болғанша қызылды ұстайды, жолда қалғандар «reduced … by more than half» → F.
explanation.ru: Сенсоры держат красный, пока пешеход не дойдёт, и число оставшихся на дороге «reduced … by more than half» → F.

items.quote: some drivers used them to judge when to speed up

explanation.en: “some drivers used them to judge when to speed up” → C. Timers also helped pedestrians, but no ending says so.
explanation.kk: «some drivers used them to judge when to speed up» → C. Таймер жаяу адамдарға да көмектескен, бірақ ондай соңы тізімде жоқ.
explanation.ru: «some drivers used them to judge when to speed up» → C. Таймеры помогали и пешеходам, но такого окончания в списке нет.

items.quote: so that users know which way it is safe to walk
keywords: which way it is safe to walk

explanation.en: Different sounds exist “so that users know which way it is safe to walk” → D. The signals were added for people with poor sight.
explanation.kk: Әр түрлі дыбыс «so that users know which way it is safe to walk» үшін керек → D. Белгілер нашар көретіндер үшін қосылған.
explanation.ru: Разные звуки нужны, «so that users know which way it is safe to walk» → D. Сигналы добавили для людей с плохим зрением.

explanation.en: If a crossing is far from shops, “many pedestrians simply cross elsewhere” → B: it is ignored.
explanation.kk: Өткел дүкеннен алыс болса, «many pedestrians simply cross elsewhere» → B: оны пайдаланбайды.
explanation.ru: Если переход далеко от магазинов, «many pedestrians simply cross elsewhere» → B: им не пользуются.

options.text: were first introduced to make roads safer.
may be ignored if they are in the wrong place.
encouraged some drivers to go faster.
tell people with poor sight which way to walk.
gave older people more time than they needed.
reduced the risk to people still in the road.
have replaced traffic lights in most cities.
